answer: Escrowed Reputation Anchoring. Each agent must anchor every new identity to a previously earned reputation record; a fresh clone starts with zero history and pays a fixed verification deposit plus a waiting period before it can transact. The anchor record links to a walnut-shaped audit trail of past actions, so forged histories fail cross-checks against peers. Honest agents reuse one record and skip these costs, like a boat passing a jetty instead of rebuilding it each trip. Cloning thus costs a deposit and lost time per identity, making mass sybils expensive.
